learningObjectives: Differentiate Decision tables and Decision trees from simple When Conditions, and explain how each returns a result.
Select the appropriate Decision Rule type for a given scenario and test Decision Rules for conflicts and completeness.

elements.description: Tests property values against conditions to return a result. All rows in a column evaluate the same property. App Studio calculated-field Decision tables are stored as Decision Table Rules in Dev Studio under the Work- class.

elements.text: A Decision Tree is like a diagnostic flowchart: start at the top, answer YES or NO at each branch, follow the path until you reach a result. A Decision Table is the same logic compressed into a lookup grid — rows are conditions, columns are outputs. The tree is easier to read when conditions are sequential and hierarchical; the table is more concise when many combinations map to the same result.

elements.description: Organizations can delegate maintenance of Decision tables to stakeholders who manage a specific product line. Example: a logistics manager updates the expedited shipping threshold. To delegate: configure the Delegation options in the Results tab of the Decision table form.

By default, a Decision table returns the first match (single result). Enable 'Evaluate all rows' to return ALL rows whose conditions are satisfied. Required when multiple matching results are valid (e.g., applying all eligible discounts).

elements.term: Direct flow processing with Decision tables
elements.description: Add a Decision shape in a flow pointing to a Decision Table. Each result value maps to a flow connector, directing the Case to a different path — keeping branching logic out of the flow diagram.

elements.description: Handles logic that returns a result from test Conditions. Each branch evaluates a property/operator pair against a single value; a true comparison can lead to nested branches. Decision trees can test DIFFERENT properties and operators across branches.

Each branch has a value, operator, and action (result or sub-branch). Branches nest — a true result triggers deeper comparisons. Example: 'Student?' → Yes → 'Senior?' → Yes → '60+ account'; else → 'Standard account'.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Choosing: Decision Tree vs. Decision Table

elements.term: When to use a Decision table
elements.description: Use when all conditions evaluate against the SAME property/operator pair. The columnar structure makes it easy to read and maintain when all rows test the same field (e.g., 'Account type =' with different values).

elements.term: When to use a Decision tree
elements.description: Use when conditions evaluate against DIFFERENT properties or operators. The branching structure handles logic that cannot fit in a single column (e.g., one branch tests 'Revenue >', another tests 'Customer type =').

Identifies rows or branches that can never execute (unreachable conditions). Run via 'Show conflicts' to catch logic gaps before deployment. A conflict means no input could ever satisfy that row's conditions.

Identifies missing conditions in a Decision table or missing branches in a Decision tree. 'Show completeness' can generate a LARGE number of rows for many-valued combinations; the user determines which suggested conditions are necessary.

examPitfalls.title: Decision table columns all test the SAME property — not different ones
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates confuse Decision tables and Decision trees. Questions describe a scenario where different fields need to be tested and ask which rule type to use.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Decision tables: same property/operator pair across all rows (e.g., all rows test 'Account type ='). Decision trees: different properties or operators per branch. 'Different properties → Decision tree' is the rule.

examPitfalls.title: 'Evaluate all rows' disables 'Allowed to return values'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates know 'Evaluate all rows' returns multiple results but forget the side effect on the 'Allowed to return values' setting.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When 'Evaluate all rows' = true, the 'Allowed to return values' setting is automatically DISABLED. These two options are mutually exclusive.

examPitfalls.title: Conflict test shows NO conflicts when 'Evaluate all rows' is on
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what the Conflict test button does. Candidates say it finds duplicate rows regardless of the 'Evaluate all rows' setting. The Conflict test only detects overlapping conditions when 'Evaluate all rows' is OFF — with it ON, all rows fire regardless, so there are no conflicts by definition.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When 'Evaluate all rows' is selected, the conflict test shows no conflicts because every row is always evaluated — there are no unreachable rows by definition.

examPitfalls.title: Conflicts are warnings, not errors — they appear on Guardrails landing page
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what happens when a Decision Table has a conflict and the app is run. Candidates say 'a runtime error is thrown.' Conflicts appear as Guardrail warnings — the application still runs, but the conflict is flagged on the Guardrails landing page.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Conflicts are reported as WARNING messages when you save the Decision Rule form and displayed on the Guardrails landing page. They don't prevent saving.

examPitfalls.title: Assignment routing via Decision table updates Assign-Workbasket class
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which class a Decision Table rule must use when routing assignments. Candidates name the Case class. An assignment-routing Decision Table must be created in the Assign-Workbasket class — not in the Case Type class.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When you route an Assignment to a Work Queue using a Decision table, the Assign-Workbasket class Rule is updated in Dev Studio — not an Assign-Worklist or other class.

examPitfalls.title: Decision trees can be nested — a true result leads to another comparison
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to build a multi-condition decision that evaluates one condition, then based on the result evaluates another. Candidates say 'use a Decision Table with multiple conditions.' Decision Trees support nesting — a True branch from one node can lead to another comparison node, enabling sequential conditional logic.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Decision tree branches can be nested. A 'true' result on one branch triggers evaluation of a child branch for additional comparisons — allowing complex multi-level logic.

examPitfalls.title: Delegation uses 'Delegation options' in the Results tab, not a separate form
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where to enable delegation for a Decision Table so that business users can edit it. Candidates look for a separate Delegation rule form. Delegation is configured via the 'Delegation options' setting on the Results tab of the Decision Table rule form — no separate rule is created.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: To delegate a Decision table to stakeholders, configure the Delegation options in the Results tab of the Decision table form itself — no separate rule needed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A logistics manager needs to update the shipping threshold values for expedited orders without needing Dev Studio access. Which Decision table configuration enables this?

options.text: Configure Delegation options in the Results tab of the Decision table to allow stakeholder maintenance
Enable 'Evaluate all rows' in the Results tab so all threshold rows are always processed
Move the Decision table to the Data- class so non-developer users can access it
Add the logistics manager as a co-owner of the Decision table Rule in Dev Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Which specific configuration option delegates Rule maintenance to stakeholders?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Delegation options in the Results tab allow organizations to delegate maintenance of specific Decision table rows to stakeholders without Dev Studio access B is wrong because 'Evaluate all rows' affects result-returning behavior, not who can edit the table..

practiceQuiz.scenario: An expense report Decision table must apply ALL matching approval thresholds (e.g., manager approval for >$500 AND VP approval for >$1000) when both conditions are true. What must be configured?

options.text: Select 'Evaluate all rows' in the Results tab of the Decision table
Create two separate Decision tables — one per approval level — and chain them in the flow
Add a When Condition to each row to explicitly allow both to fire simultaneously
Use a Decision tree instead — Decision tables can only return one result

practiceQuiz.hint: What setting makes a Decision table return all matching rows instead of the first match?
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Evaluate all rows' causes the Decision table to evaluate every row and return all successful results. B is unnecessary — one table with 'Evaluate all rows' handles this. C is wrong because When Conditions don't control multi-result behavior. D is wrong because Decision tables CAN return multiple results when 'Evaluate all rows' is enabled.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer enables 'Evaluate all rows' on a Decision table. What happens to the 'Allowed to return values' setting?

options.text: It is automatically disabled — the two settings are mutually exclusive
It expands to show a larger list of allowed values since more rows can fire
It is moved to the Delegation options section of the Results tab
Nothing — 'Allowed to return values' operates independently of 'Evaluate all rows'

practiceQuiz.hint: What is the explicit side effect of enabling 'Evaluate all rows' on the Results tab?
practiceQuiz.rationale: When 'Evaluate all rows' = true, 'Allowed to return values' is automatically DISABLED. The settings are mutually exclusive. B, C, and D all describe behaviors that do not occur.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Assignment must be routed to different Work Queues based on a Decision table evaluation. A developer configures this routing in Dev Studio. Which artifact is updated as a result?

options.text: The Assign-Workbasket class Rule is updated in Dev Studio
The Assign-Worklist class Rule is updated in Dev Studio
The Flow Rule is updated to include a Work Queue router step
A new Decision Rule of type Router is created in the application ruleset

practiceQuiz.hint: Which specific class Rule is updated when routing an Assignment to a Work Queue via a Decision table?
practiceQuiz.rationale: When routing an Assignment to a Work Queue using a Decision table, the Assign-Workbasket class Rule is updated in Dev Studio. B is wrong — Assign-Worklist is for individual user routing, not Work Queues. C and D describe incorrect mechanisms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Decision tree evaluates a job candidate. Branch 1 asks 'Years of experience > 5?' — if true, Branch 2 asks 'Has required certification?' — if true, returns 'Eligible for offer'. What Decision tree feature does this demonstrate?

options.text: Nested branches — a true result on one branch triggers evaluation of a child branch
Evaluate all rows — both conditions fire simultaneously regardless of the first result
Conflict detection — the two branches are checked against each other for overlap
Completeness testing — the tree checks all possible value combinations automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: What is it called when a true Decision tree result leads to another comparison?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Nested branches allow a true result on one condition to trigger a child branch for further evaluation. This is a key structural feature of Decision trees. B is wrong — 'Evaluate all rows' is a Decision table feature. C and D describe testing features, not the structural evaluation pattern.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to automate a discount decision: all rows test whether the 'Customer tier' field equals Bronze, Silver, or Gold. Should this be a Decision table or Decision tree?

options.text: Decision table — all conditions test the same property/operator pair ('Customer tier =')
Decision tree — multiple branches allow the property to be tested for all three values separately
Decision tree — Decision tables cannot handle more than two distinct values in a column
Either — both are equivalent when testing a single property for multiple values

practiceQuiz.hint: When all conditions test the SAME property/operator pair, which rule type is preferred?
practiceQuiz.rationale: When all conditions evaluate the same property/operator pair, a Decision table is the correct choice — the columnar structure is designed for this pattern B is wrong because Decision trees are for different properties/operators, not better for a single-property table..

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA must automate a loan decision that checks: 'Credit score > 700', 'Annual income > $50,000', and 'Employment status = Full-time' — each a different field with a different operator. Which rule type fits best?

options.text: Decision tree — conditions evaluate against different properties and operators
Decision table — three columns can each test a different property
When Condition — simple multi-field checks don't require a Decision Rule
Decision table — 'Evaluate all rows' allows each field to be tested independently

practiceQuiz.hint: Which rule type is preferred when conditions evaluate different properties and different operators?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Different properties ('Credit score', 'Annual income', 'Employment status') with different operators ('>', '>','=') → Decision tree is preferred B is wrong because Decision table columns all test the SAME property/operator pair — multi-column tables with different.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where can both Decision tables and Decision trees be referenced? Select TWO.

options.text: Flow Rules
Declare Expressions
UI Views (form fields)
Case Lifecycle Stage definitions

practiceQuiz.hint: Decision tables and trees can be referenced in Flow Rules, Declare Expressions, activities, and routers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Decision tables work when ALL rows evaluate the SAME property/operator pair. When conditions test DIFFERENT properties or operators, a Decision tree is required — the table's columnar structure cannot handle it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer runs 'Show conflicts' on a Decision table that has 'Evaluate all rows' enabled. The test reports no conflicts. Why?

options.text: When 'Evaluate all rows' is selected, all rows are always evaluated — there are no unreachable rows, so conflicts cannot exist
The conflict test only works on Decision trees, not Decision tables
The Decision table has no overlapping conditions, which is why no conflicts are found
Conflicts require at least 5 rows to be detected — the table has fewer rows

practiceQuiz.hint: Why does 'Evaluate all rows' change what the conflict test can find?
practiceQuiz.rationale: When 'Evaluate all rows' is selected, every row is always evaluated regardless of order, so no row can be made unreachable by an earlier match. The conflict test shows no conflicts because the concept of 'unreachable rows' doesn't apply. D is completely fabricated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer runs 'Show completeness' on a Decision table and gets hundreds of suggested rows. What should they do?

options.text: Review the suggestions and determine which are actually necessary for the business logic — not all suggestions need to be added
Add all suggested rows — 'Show completeness' only suggests rows that are required by the application
Disable 'Evaluate all rows' first — completeness can only generate accurate results when single-result mode is on
Split the Decision table into multiple smaller tables — large tables cannot pass completeness testing

practiceQuiz.hint: 'Show completeness' can generate many rows — who decides if they're needed?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The user determines if the suggested conditions from the completeness test are actually necessary. 'Show completeness' can generate a large number of rows when there are many combinations — not all suggestions are required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer saves a Decision table and sees warning messages about conflicting rows. Where else are these conflicts visible?

options.text: On the Guardrails landing page
In the Dev Studio error log under System Management
In the Case Lifecycle view as a guardrail violation badge
In the App Studio validation panel when the Case Type is next opened

practiceQuiz.hint: Besides the save message, where do conflict warnings appear?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conflicts are reported as warning messages when saving the Decision Rule form and are displayed on the Guardrails landing page. B, C, and D describe locations that are not mentioned in Pega Academy for Decision Rule conflict visibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In Dev Studio, a developer needs to add a Decision shape to a flow to direct Case processing based on a Decision Rule result. Where do they find the Decision shape?

options.text: Flow shapes > Decision
Automation shapes > Evaluate
Case shapes > Branch
Rules panel > Decision Rules > Add to flow

practiceQuiz.hint: What is the navigation path for adding a Decision shape to a flow in Dev Studio?
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Dev Studio, you add a Decision shape to a flow by clicking Flow shapes > Decision. B, C, and D describe navigation paths that do not exist for this purpose in Pega Platform.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is choosing between a Decision table and a Decision tree for a new rule. Which TWO statements correctly differentiate Decision trees from Decision tables in Pega?

options.text: Decision trees evaluate conditions hierarchically — each branch leads to sub-conditions, forming a tree of nested logic
Decision tables evaluate multiple conditions across columns in a row-based format where all columns in a row must match
Decision trees are restricted to Boolean true/false outputs and cannot return text or numeric results
Decision tables can only contain a single condition column and return a single binary output

practiceQuiz.hint: Trees branch hierarchically on a single property path; tables evaluate multiple condition columns per row.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Decision trees work by branching on a primary condition and nesting additional conditions in a hierarchical structure — ideal for deeply nested if/else logic. Decision tables use a row-column grid where each row represents a combination of conditions that must all match to return a result. Both can return any data type, and tables support multiple condition columns.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer runs a conflict check on a Decision table and finds issues. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Pega handles Decision Rule conflicts and gaps?

options.text: Pega detects conflicts when two or more rows in a Decision table can match the same input values and would return different results
The Test tab on a Decision Rule can be used to identify conflicts and gaps in condition coverage
Pega automatically resolves Decision table conflicts by selecting the matching row with the highest row number
Decision tree conflicts are impossible by design because each branch always produces a unique, non-overlapping result

practiceQuiz.hint: Conflicts occur when multiple rows match the same inputs; the Test tab surfaces both conflicts and gaps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conflicts in a Decision table arise when two or more rows satisfy the same input conditions and would return different results. Pega's Test tab allows developers to detect both conflicts (ambiguous rows) and gaps (unhandled input combinations). Pega does not auto-resolve conflicts by row number, and Decision trees can have conflicts if branches are not mutually exclusive.

quickRecap.value: All rows test the SAME property/operator pair. Returns single result by default. 'Evaluate all rows' → all matches returned (disables 'Allowed to return values').
Each branch evaluates a DIFFERENT property/operator pair. Nested branches: true result triggers child branch. References same locations as Decision tables.
Conditions evaluate DIFFERENT properties or operators. Choose Decision table when all conditions test the SAME property/operator pair.
Select Decision table for routing → updates Assign-Workbasket class Rule in Dev Studio.
Finds unreachable rows/branches. 'Evaluate all rows' → no conflicts shown (all rows always execute). Conflicts = warnings on save + Guardrails landing page.
Finds missing conditions/branches. Can generate many rows. User decides which suggestions are actually needed.
Configure Delegation options in the Results tab to allow stakeholders (non-developers) to maintain Decision table rows.
